title: A tap with tape on it

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Can you fix things at home? Guess: what is wrong in Sam's kitchen?

chapters.title: Drip, drip, drip
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 1 SCENE: a small kitchen at night, a red-haired bearded man in pyjamas staring at a dripping kitchen tap wrapped in grey tape, a bucket under it

chapters.title: Grandmother's radio
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 2 SCENE: a warm old living room, an old wooden radio on a lace tablecloth, an elderly grandfather with white hair fixing a loose knob with a tiny screwdriver, NOT the podcast hosts

chapters.title: Worn-out shoes
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 3 SCENE: a doorstep, a red-haired bearded man gluing the sole of a very old running shoe, a woman with round glasses and a lavender sweater shaking her head and smiling

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is fixing things. Leyla, are you handy at home?
Not really. When something breaks, I call my neighbour, Mr Aliyev. He can repair anything.
Lucky you. I need someone like that.
[laugh] He has more tools than a shop.
Well, I need him. My kitchen tap has a leak. Drip, drip, drip, all night.
Oh no. What did you do?
I put tape around it. A temporary fix. That was three months ago.
[chuckle] Three months is not temporary, Sam!
I know. The real problem is a spare part. The shop says it comes from Germany.
My grandmother never throws anything away. Her old radio is fifty years old, and it still works.
How?
My grandad repaired it again and again. When a button was loose, he fixed it with a tiny screw.
Things lasted longer back then. Now a phone feels old after three years.
That's true. Do you repair your own things?
Only my running shoes. They're completely worn out, but I glued the sole back on.
Sam! Your half marathon is soon. Don't cut corners with your shoes.
You're right. A cheap repair could cost me a broken ankle.
So — new shoes this week?
New shoes. And maybe I'll finally call Mr Aliyev about the tap.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what was the last thing you fixed yourself — and how did it go?
Mine is a tap with tape on it. See you next time!
Bye for now!
